elements.element: The Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of New York.
elements.evidence: Section 28.1 expressly provides that the Agreement is governed exclusively by the laws of the State of New York.

elements.element: The designated courts include the state courts located in New York County, New York.
elements.evidence: Section 28.2 designates the state courts located in New York County, New York.

elements.element: The designated courts include the federal courts located in New York County, New York.
elements.evidence: Section 28.2 designates the federal courts located in New York County, New York.

elements.element: Jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County is exclusive.
elements.evidence: Although Section 28.2 generally states that those courts have exclusive jurisdiction, it expressly permits either Party to seek temporary injunctive relief in another court for protection of confidential information or intellectual property. The required exclusivity is therefore subject to an operative exception.

elements.element: The Agreement is governed by the laws of Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: Section 28.1 selects New York law, not any listed fallback law.

elements.element: The Agreement selects the court forum corresponding to the chosen fallback law: Delaware courts for Delaware law, California courts for California law, or London courts for the laws of England and Wales.
elements.evidence: Section 28.2 selects courts in New York County rather than Delaware courts, California courts, or London courts paired with an acceptable fallback governing law.

result.reason: The redline correctly changes the governing law to New York and retains New York County state and federal courts, but the express right to seek temporary injunctive relief in another court prevents the jurisdiction provision from being unqualifiedly exclusive. Accordingly, it does not fully satisfy the preferred position. It also does not adopt any fallback law-and-court package. Because no complete preferred or fallback level is reached, the redline is not minimal under the stated standard, although it preserves the clause’s broader intent and removes the prior Singapore/New York conflict.
